papers.title: Information, Mass, Energy Principles: A biophysical and ecological framework for understanding the brain.
papers.reason: The paper offers a broad biophysical framework for brain organization with some relevance through inhibitory-control performance and neurodegeneration modelling, but executive function is not its central object.

papers.title: Association of high-frequency repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation with 6-month cognitive outcomes and white matter lesion progression in patients with cerebral small vessel disease and cognitive impairment.
papers.reason: The title indicates a clinical cognitive-outcome study in cognitive impairment, but there is no specific evidence here of executive-function modelling, task-based assessment, or mechanistic cognitive findings.

papers.title: Expectation-driven gain modulation of preparatory spatial attention
papers.reason: This is a central human EEG and behavioural study of preparatory spatial attention, using inverted encoding models to characterize attentional gain mechanisms relevant to computational modelling.

papers.title: Social Anxiety Modulates Default Mode Network Dysfunction and Working Memory Impairment During Social Media‐Like Cue Distraction
papers.reason: The paper directly studies working memory impairment under distraction with fMRI network measures and individual differences in social anxiety, making it substantially relevant to executive-function mechanisms.

papers.title: Working memory neural correlates after ketamine in treatment-resistant depression: a randomized placebo-controlled functional magnetic resonance imaging study.
papers.reason: This human clinical fMRI study examines working-memory task activation in treatment-resistant depression after ketamine, but its mechanistic contribution to executive-function modelling is limited by secondary exploratory analyses.

papers.title: Effects of virtual reality and exergame interventions on cognitive function in Chinese older adults with cognitive impairment: A three-level meta-analysis.
papers.reason: This is a broad meta-analysis of cognitive intervention effects in older adults with cognitive impairment, with no clear focus on executive-function modelling or task-based digital biomarker classification.

papers.title: The computational mechanism of stroboscopic training in enhancing badminton anticipation: a randomized controlled trial
papers.reason: The paper appears to model or analyze mechanisms of human perceptual anticipation and attention in a randomized training study, but its sports-specific focus makes it only partially aligned with executive-function modelling.
